explain.say: Have you ever watched waves at the beach? They rise up, crash, and roll away, and then another one comes. Feelings work just like that! Look at the wavy line on the board. It shows how strong a feeling is over time.

faq.a: No. Feelings rise, peak and fade, like waves. Even very big feelings get smaller with time, though some may come back now and then.
asks: Will this feeling ever go away?

faq.q: How can I ride out a big feeling?
faq.a: Notice it, name it, take slow breaths, and remind yourself it will pass. Doing something calming, like drawing or a walk, helps the wave roll by.
asks: How do I get through a big feeling?

faq.q: Why do feelings keep coming back?
faq.a: Reminders, tiredness or new events can bring a feeling back. That is normal. Each time you ride it, you get a little better at handling it.
asks: Why does my sadness come back?

faq.q: Should I try to stop a feeling?
faq.a: Pushing a feeling away often makes it come back stronger. It usually works better to let yourself feel it, while choosing safe things to do.

faq.q: What if a feeling never seems to pass?
faq.a: If you feel sad, worried or angry most days for weeks, talk to a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. They can help.
asks: My bad feeling will not go away

facts: In a famous 1987 study, people told not to think about a white bear thought about it more often, showing that pushing thoughts away can make them come back.
"Urge surfing" is a skill taught by psychologists to help people let strong feelings rise and pass without acting on them.
